summary: Frontend test at 390x844 as user_avatar_test, using the camera mock (/app/tests/cam_mock_avatar.js) plus a new lens mock (/app/tests/cam_mock_lens.js). The lens mock fakes the track label, enumerateDevices, getSettings, getCapabilities zoom{0.5,10} and records applyConstraints. (1) openNormalLens PASS with English labels. Single mode, back camera: the first getUserMedia call (facingMode environment) returns 'Back Ultra Wide Camera', then a second call is made with deviceId exact 'back-id' ('Back Camera'), and applyConstraints({advanced:[{zoom:1}]}) runs on 'Back Camera'. Double mode, flipped to front with a normal 'Front Camera' default: only 1 getUserMedia call, zoom 1 applied. Flipped back in double mode: switches to 'Back Camera' again. Front with a 'Front Ultra Wide Camera' default: switches to deviceId 'front-id'. The video stream is active and nothing crashed. Switching the mode alone does not reopen the stream; this is expected, since the lens is already the normal one. FAIL with Italian iOS labels: with the default 'Fotocamera tripla posteriore' and 'Fotocamera posteriore' present, there is no switch (see action items). (2) keepRealProportions. GOOD upper+lower: no warnings, but the clamp now changes the result. The posted inseam_r is 0.4558, which gives leg_frac exactly 0.530 (the clamp's upper limit). Measurements are now chest 81 / waist 70 / hips 96 / shoulder 37 / inseam 77, versus 76/66/90/33/83 in iteration 27, so the result is NOT unchanged. The same subject in a single full-body photo has a real leg_frac of 0.556 (heels), so the 0.53 cap cuts off real proportions. Compared with single-shot (79/67/91/35/80), hips are 5.5% higher, outside the 5% target. STRETCHED lower (x1.6), and also x1.3: the pose anchor fails, so reg is null and keepRealProportions NEVER RUNS. The code then falls back to stacking photo 2 under photo 1, giving a 960x2000 avatar with the dress duplicated and very long legs. The only warning is no_measure, features=null, and measurements are not updated (inseam keeps its old value of 77-80, which is plausible only because nothing was recomputed). The requirement 'stitched avatar must NOT show super-long legs' FAILS. (3) Regression: single 1-photo fullbody.jpg works: POST with features, measurements 79/67/91/35/80, method auto_photo. 2-shot never blocks: 0 avatar-photo-issue in every case, and the save always succeeds.

ui_bugs.issue: When the lower photo's pose or hips are not detected (reproduced with lower.jpg stretched vertically x1.3 and x1.6), reg is null. keepRealProportions is skipped and the 'stack photo 2 under photo 1' fallback produces a 960x2000 avatar with the dress drawn twice and very long legs. This is exactly the stretched figure the fix is meant to prevent.

The upper limit of 0.53 is too tight. On the good upper+lower pair it engages (leg_frac clamped from about 0.55 to 0.530), which shrinks bodyH and raises every width ratio. Chest/waist/hips go from 76/66/90 to 81/70/96, so the result is changed versus before. The real leg_frac of the same subject from the single photo is 0.556.

The regex only covers English labels. Italian iOS labels ('Fotocamera tripla posteriore', 'Fotocamera doppia grandangolare posteriore') are not treated as non-normal, so no switch to 'Fotocamera posteriore' happens. This was verified with the mock. The 'ultra' and 'tele' patterns do match.

integration_issues.issue: The toast says 'Avatar salvato: misure stimate da altezza e peso', but no quick-estimate is called (body is empty because the height is already in the profile). The old photo-based measurements are left as they are.

action_items: pose.js: also apply real proportions when there is no anchor. In the stacking fallback, size the lower photo so that the legs take about 0.5 of the height. Better still, when l.p or the hips are missing, cut the lower photo at its own waist (top) rather than stacking the whole frame under the upper one, so the torso is not duplicated. Alternatively, warn and offer to redo the legs instead of saving a 2000px-tall figure.
pose.js: widen LEG_FRAC to about [0.44, 0.58], or apply it only when the error is large (for example frac > 0.6 or < 0.42), so that good stitches (real 0.55-0.56 with heels) stay unchanged.

AvatarCamera.jsx: extend NOT_NORMAL_LENS for Italian/localized iOS labels, for example /ultra|wide|dual|doppia|triple|tripla|grandangol|tele|0[.,]5|macro/i. Keep 'Fotocamera posteriore' and 'Fotocamera anteriore' as normal.

AvatarCamera.jsx (risk, not verified on a device): on iOS virtual dual/triple devices, zoom 1 is the 0.5x ultra-wide (UI 1x is zoom 2). Forcing zoom:1 when no physical normal lens is found could LOCK the ultra-wide. Apply zoom 1 only after switching to a physical normal lens, or only when the label is normal.
AvatarBox: when no_measure appears and a height is saved, call /profile/quick-estimate, or reword the toast.
critical_code_review_comments: keepRealProportions measures the leg as reg.t + l.bottom*reg.s - u.hipY, and the shoes/heels are included in l.bottom, so heels push the fraction above 0.53 and trigger the clamp.
keepRealProportions scales the lower photo uniformly. A lower photo that is truly stretched only vertically keeps its aspect distortion; this is fine because the scale is limited.
openNormalLens: the side regex is applied to device labels, which are empty before permission. This is fine because enumerateDevices is called after getUserMedia.

success_rate.frontend: 60% (lens switch and zoom PASS for English labels; single-shot regression PASS; never-block PASS; good 2-shot changed versus before; stretched lower FAIL)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Load cam_mock_avatar.js (replace __IMGS__) and then cam_mock_lens.js in the same init script. rca of the issue: Stretched lower photo: extractTwoPartRatios applies keepRealProportions only inside the branch `if (u.p && l.p && hips visible)`. When MediaPipe does not anchor the distorted lower photo, reg stays null and the fallback `{s: u.W/l.W, t: u.H, seam: u.H}` stacks the full lower frame, waist included, under the full upper frame. The result is a duplicated torso and long legs. Good photos changed: LEG_FRAC[1]=0.53 is below this subject's real hip-to-floor fraction with heels (0.556), so the clamp rescales good stitches.
